speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; please describe the skin lesion you are concerned about, including its location, how long it has been there, and if it is changing in size, shape, or color.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the location of these lesions, combined with your heavy smoking history and lack of response to prior treatments, is concerning. Have either of these lesions been bleeding, ulcerating, or growing in size over the last few months?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the non-healing, crusty, and painless nature of these lesions on your penile shaft and finger, along with your smoking history, I am highly concerned for a malignancy such as squamous cell carcinoma. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I need to see the physical appearance of these spots. REQUEST IMAGES: Penile_shaft and Left_middle_finger dermoscopy. REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count and Hepatitis B/C serology.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Dermatological Examination: Inspection reveals an erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders on the dorsal penile shaft and left middle finger; Palpation shows lesions are firm, non-tender, and without warmth; Regional Lymph Nodes show no palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel: Syphilis Negative, HIV Negative, HBV Negative, HCV Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Cutaneous). The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusted, erythematous lesions on sun-exposed skin and the penis, combined with significant smoking history, firm non-tender masses, and biopsy results showing cellular atypia (hyperchromasia, multinucleation, increased mitosis), confirms this malignancy. The negative STD panel rules out infectious etiologies like syphilis or herpes.
